issue: The key uses pre-ASU 2016-14 terminology: "(c) Only in unrestricted net assets", and its explanation says "Expenses decrease unrestricted net assets." Elsewhere in the same module, far-nfs-22(a) teaches that "unrestricted, temporary, permanent" is "the old model", and far-nfs-17(d) and -23(d) key "temporarily/permanently restricted" as outdated-rule traps. A candidate who learned the current terms may hesitate over a key worded in superseded terms.
evidence: ASU 2016-14 replaced "unrestricted net assets" with "net assets without donor restrictions" (ASC 958-210-45-1, 958-225-45-7). The lesson, the item explanation and every other item use the current term; only this key and its rationale do not.
fix: Change (c) to "Only as decreases in net assets without donor restrictions", and change its explanation to "Correct. All expenses are reported as decreases in net assets without donor restrictions; restricted resources are first released (reclassified)."

issue: The correct-choice explanation is a non sequitur: "(a) As a reclassification between classes. Correct. Expenses are reported there." "There" has no referent, and the explanation does not say which classes or why. Distractor (d) "Only in the notes" carries trap "partial-computation" on a non-computational item.
evidence: The key is right (ASC 958-205-45-9: a release is a reclassification from net assets with donor restrictions to net assets without donor restrictions, reported as "net assets released from restrictions"). The explanation as written does not teach this.
fix: Rewrite (a)'s explanation: "Correct. Spending $80,000 on the program satisfies the purpose restriction, so $80,000 is reclassified from net assets with donor restrictions to net assets without donor restrictions (net assets released from restrictions), where the $80,000 program expense is reported." Retag (d) as "wrong-rule".

issue: Duplicate items: both stems are identical ("What liquidity information must an NFP disclose?") and both keys say "Assets available within a year/within one year". The key wording is imprecise: the requirement covers financial assets available to meet cash needs for general expenditures within one year of the balance-sheet date. far-nfs-27's distractors ("Nothing beyond the balance sheet", "Only the current ratio", "Only restricted cash") are implausible, and its key is the only option without an absolute ("only", "nothing").
evidence: cues.md: Jaccard 1.00 for far-nfs-14 ~ far-nfs-27. ASC 958-210-50-1A requires qualitative information on how the NFP manages liquid resources and quantitative information on the availability of financial assets at the balance-sheet date to meet cash needs for general expenditures within one year. "Assets" (not "financial assets") and the missing "for general expenditures" make the key text loose. far-nfs-06 already tests the quantitative application.
fix: Keep far-nfs-14 with the key reworded to "Qualitative and quantitative information about financial assets available to meet general expenditures within one year". Replace far-nfs-27 with a scenario item, for example a draft liquidity table that wrongly includes perpetual endowment corpus and a donor-restricted pledge due in two years, asking which amount must be removed.

issue: Near-duplicate computations (with far-nfs-03 and the lesson's worked and faded examples). Distractors and explanations are weak. In far-nfs-19, (b) $450,000 and (c) $150,000 match no stated misconception, and (c) is explained only as "Not the computation." (a) $50,000 decrease is the omit-releases error (500 - 550), not a sign error as its trap "wrong-sign" says. In far-nfs-26, (d) $40,000 is "Not the computation." Neither item-level explanation shows the computation.
evidence: far-nfs-19: 500,000 + 100,000 - 550,000 = +50,000. Omitting releases gives -50,000 (= (a)). A sign error on releases (500 - 100 - 550) gives -150,000, which is not offered. 450,000 and 150,000 cannot be derived from any one error. far-nfs-26: 500,000 + 40,000 - 450,000 = +90,000. Item explanation is only "Releases from restriction increase net assets without donor restrictions." cues.md: far-nfs-19 ~ far-nfs-26 Jaccard 0.50.
fix: Keep one of the two. In the one kept, replace the arbitrary distractors with error-derived ones: for far-nfs-19, $150,000 decrease (releases subtracted), $50,000 decrease (releases omitted), $650,000 increase (expenses ignored). Retag (a) as partial-computation, and put the full computation in the item explanation ("500,000 + 100,000 released - 550,000 = 50,000 increase").

Example: give a prior-year restricted gift, current-year spending partly funded by unrestricted cash (the ASC 958-205-45 both-available rule), and other revenues and expenses, and ask for the change in each net asset class. issue: Trap labels do not match the misconception the distractor models. far-nfs-02(b), "Over the building's useful life as it is depreciated": tagged overgeneralization, but this was the pre-ASU 2016-14 implied-time-restriction policy option, so the trap is outdated-rule, and the explanation does not say so. far-nfs-06(c), $800,000 (includes the donor-restricted pledge): tagged partial-computation, but it is a classification error. far-nfs-08(a), "Without donor restrictions, because the income is unrestricted": tagged partial-computation on a non-computational classification item.
evidence: Before ASU 2016-14, an NFP could adopt a policy of implying a time restriction on long-lived assets bought with restricted gifts and releasing it over the asset's useful life. ASU 2016-14 removed that option and requires the placed-in-service approach absent explicit donor stipulations (ASC 958-205-45-12). The other two retags follow from the explanations' own wording ("includes the restricted pledge"; "the corpus is restricted in perpetuity"). Related trap mislabels in far-nfs-16(d) and far-nfs-19(a) are covered in those items' own findings.
source: ASU 2016-14 (BC on placed-in-service); ASC 958-205-45-12
fix: Retag far-nfs-02(b) as outdated-rule, with the explanation "Before ASU 2016-14 an NFP could elect to release such gifts over the asset's useful life; that option was eliminated, so the release occurs when the asset is placed in service." Retag far-nfs-06(c) and far-nfs-08(a) as wrong-classification.

issue: Key text is vague and garbled: "(a) All four statements, including expenses". It does not name the four, and "including expenses" is unclear. It is also the longest option. The item repeats far-nfs-chk2, far-nfs-10 and flashcard fc1 (required statements) with no new angle.
evidence: The four required presentations are the statement of financial position, statement of activities, statement of cash flows, and analysis of expenses by function and nature, which may be a separate statement, on the face of the statement of activities, or in the notes (ASC 958-205-45-4 to 45-6). The choice text leaves the candidate to infer which four. cues.md flags "key longest".
fix: Retire far-nfs-21 (covered by far-nfs-10, far-nfs-chk2 and fc1). Or rewrite the choices as explicit parallel sets, e.g., (a) Financial position, activities, cash flows, and an analysis of expenses by function and nature [key]; (b) Financial position, activities and cash flows only; (c) Financial position, activities, and changes in fund balances; (d) Activities, cash flows, and functional expenses only.

issue: Stem is incomplete for a difficulty-3 analysis item. It does not say that the remaining $300,000 of investments is free of donor restrictions and liquid within one year, or that the $120,000 of receivables is unrestricted. Under UPMIFA, the accumulated gains of a donor-restricted endowment are with donor restrictions until appropriated, so "investments $900,000 of which $600,000 is perpetual endowment corpus" does not by itself make the other $300,000 available.
evidence: Key: 300,000 + 120,000 + (900,000 - 600,000) = 720,000 (recomputed; agrees). The explanation calls the $300,000 "unrestricted investments", but the stem never says so. If any of it is unappropriated endowment return or illiquid (e.g., lock-up funds), it is excluded from availability (ASC 958-210-50-1A; ASC 958-205-45, UPMIFA).
source: ASC 958-210-50-1A; ASC 958-205-45 (endowment return under UPMIFA)
fix: Reword: "investments $900,000, of which $600,000 is perpetual endowment corpus and $300,000 is unrestricted, readily marketable securities; receivables (without donor restrictions) due in 6 months $120,000; ..."

issue: The lesson never teaches the rule that, when an expense is incurred for a purpose for which both restricted and unrestricted resources are available, the restriction is released to the extent of the expense (far-nfs-09 tests it at difficulty 3). The worked example's wording "youth program expenses paid from restricted gifts 90,000" suggests that releases depend on which cash paid the expense, which is exactly the misconception far-nfs-09(a) traps.
evidence: Lesson body, "Releases from restriction": "When the donor's purpose is fulfilled or the time passes, the NFP reclassifies the amount" (no both-available rule). Worked example scenario: "youth program expenses paid from restricted gifts 90,000; other program expenses 380,000". far-nfs-09 key: $25,000 released even though "the NFP spent $40,000 of unrestricted resources".
source: ASC 958-205-45 (release of restrictions; expense incurred for a purpose for which both classes are available)
fix: Add one sentence under "Releases from restriction": "If the NFP incurs an expense for a purpose for which both restricted and unrestricted resources are available, the restriction is released to the extent of the expense, regardless of which cash was used." Reword the worked example to "youth program expenses (a program for which restricted gifts are available) 90,000".

issue: Endowment topics tested by this module's items are not taught in the lesson body. These are UPMIFA classification of endowment return (with donor restrictions until appropriated; far-nfs-08 explanation, far-nfs-20, far-nfs-24), the term "quasi-endowment" (far-nfs-17, -23), and net presentation of investment return (far-nfs-05, -28, fc6; mentioned only in Key Takeaways). The next module (far-nfp-revenue) does not cover them either.
evidence: grep of lesson.md: "endowment" appears only in the mermaid node "Perpetual (endowment corpus)", the board-designated trap, and the cash-flow bullets. "UPMIFA", "appropriat", "quasi" and "investment return" (outside the takeaway) do not appear. grep of far-nfp-revenue/lesson.md: no UPMIFA, appropriation or quasi-endowment text.
source: ASC 958-205-45 (UPMIFA endowment classification); ASC 958-225-45-14
fix: Add a short "Endowments and investment return" section. Cover: donor-restricted endowment corpus (with donor restrictions, perpetual); return on a donor-restricted endowment (with donor restrictions until appropriated under UPMIFA, then released); board-designated or quasi-endowment (without donor restrictions); investment return reported net of external and direct internal investment expenses. Add one inline check.

issue: The big-idea example and the JE memo contradict the body's placed-in-service rule for long-lived assets. Big idea: the food bank's $200,000 restricted to buy a refrigerated truck is released "When it spends the money". JE memo: "The expense itself (or the asset purchase) is recorded in net assets without donor restrictions" (an asset purchase is not recorded in net assets).
evidence: Body: "A gift of cash restricted to buy a long-lived asset is released when the asset is placed in service (absent other donor stipulations)" (ASC 958-205-45-12). For a truck, purchase and placing in service usually coincide, but the bigIdea teaches the spending trigger first, and far-nfs-02 then keys placed-in-service.
fix: Big idea: "When it buys the truck and places it in service, the restriction is released and the amount moves to without donor restrictions." JE memo: "The expense (or, for a restricted asset purchase, the asset once placed in service) is reported in net assets without donor restrictions."

issue: Liquidity is stated twice (the "Liquidity disclosures" section and again under "Notes") but never worked numerically, although far-nfs-06 (analysis, difficulty 3) requires computing available financial assets. The Statement of financial position topic (Blueprint FAR I.B.1) also gets little body coverage (e.g., disclosure of board designations, net presentation of underwater endowments in net assets with donor restrictions).
evidence: Lesson sections "Liquidity disclosures" and "Notes" repeat the same sentence with no table. Blueprint FAR Area I group B has topics for the statement of financial position, statement of activities, statement of cash flows and notes (review/reference/blueprint-notes.md).
source: ASC 958-210-50-1A; ASC 958-210-50-3; ASC 958-205-50 (underwater endowments)
fix: Merge the two liquidity passages and add a small faded table: total financial assets less perpetual corpus, less donor-restricted receivables, less board designations (with an explanation that they can be undesignated), giving the amount available within one year.

The lesson's objectives and line 34 also say '(management and general; fundraising)'. Found in the orchestrator spot-check; the batch reviewer listed fc5 as no-issue.

issue: Skill and difficulty labels are inflated across the module. Every item from far-nfr-21 to far-nfr-28, plus 09, 10, 17 and far-x1-16, is labeled analysis/difficulty 3, but none of them needs analysis. Three are pure recall (09, 24, 27), which is two levels off. Because 12 of the module's 30 practice and exam MCQs are tagged analysis, the Blueprint skill-mix figures are skewed.
evidence: far-nfr-18 (application, d2) and far-nfr-24 (analysis, d3) are the same item: 500 hours of unskilled envelope stuffing, keyed 'not recognized'. far-nfr-17 (analysis, d3) and far-x1-34 (application, d2) are the same $100,000 matching-gift fact pattern. 09 asks for the recall-level rule (a barrier and a right of return are both required); 27 asks for the recall-level fact that spending restricted cash releases the restriction; 28 asks whether dues equal to benefits are exchange revenue. 25 is one multiplication, 500 x (200-80) = 60,000. x1-16 is one subtraction, 50,000 - 30,000 = 20,000. 26 is a 3-period PV. The Blueprint tasks for this topic (FAR-III.C.5 R&U, FAR-III.C.6 Application, FAR-I.B.2.3 Application in review/reference/blueprint-tasks.csv) are below analysis, and the analysis verbs (analyze, reconcile, detect/investigate/correct) apply to none of these items. Label counts in cues.md: analysis 12, application 16, remembering 2.
source: AICPA 2026 Blueprint skill definitions; review/reference/blueprint-notes.md (FAR skill allocation and verb conventions)
fix: Relabel as follows. 09 remembering d1. 24 remembering d1. 27 remembering d1. 10 application d2. 17 application d2 (match far-x1-34). 21 application d2. 22 application d1. 23 application d2. 25 application d2. 26 application d2. 28 application d1. far-x1-16 application d2. If the module should keep any analysis items, write true analysis items instead, such as correcting a draft statement of activities that misclassifies a conditional grant and contributed services.

issue: The GAAS rule for departing from a presumptively mandatory ("should") requirement is taught as "comply unless an alternative achieves the objective". That is not the AU-C 200 test. The key takeaway, the worked example (scenario: the auditor "believes an alternative procedure achieves the same objective", so the answer is "Yes, depart"), the aud-ps-chk2 key ("must be followed unless a documented departure meets the objective"), the aud-ps-10 stem ("departs ... because an alternative procedure better achieves its objective") and the aud-x1-29 explanation all teach that an equally good or better alternative justifies a departure.
evidence: AU-C 200.25-.26: the auditor must comply with a presumptively mandatory requirement in all cases where it is relevant, except in rare circumstances. Departure "is expected to arise only when the requirement is for a specific procedure to be performed and, in the specific circumstances of the audit, that procedure would be ineffective in achieving the intent of the requirement". The auditor then performs alternative procedures to achieve the intent. AU-C 230.13 requires documenting the justification and how the alternatives achieve the intent. Whether an alternative is "better" or "the same" is not a ground for departure. Only the PCAOB test (Rule 3101(a)(2): alternative actions sufficient to achieve the objectives, shown by verifiable, objective, documented evidence) resembles the lesson wording. The lesson presents the rule as GAAS, and chk2 and x1-29 explicitly ask about GAAS. A candidate who learns this will pick "when an alternative procedure achieves the same objective" on an exam question about when a GAAS departure is allowed.
fix: Lesson takeaway: "\"Should\" = presumptively mandatory. Comply except in rare circumstances where the specified procedure would be ineffective in achieving the requirement's intent. Then perform alternative procedures that achieve the intent, and document the justification (AU-C 200.26, AU-C 230.13). The PCAOB allows a departure only with verifiable, objective, documented evidence that the alternative was sufficient (Rule 3101)." Worked example: make the scenario one in which the specified procedure would be ineffective in the circumstances. chk2 (c): "It must be followed except in rare circumstances, with a justified, documented departure". aud-ps-10 stem: "...because, in the circumstances, the required procedure would be ineffective in achieving its intent". aud-x1-29 explanation: replace "an alternative achieves the objective" with the ineffective-procedure condition.

issue: The lesson cites PCAOB Rule 3101 for the categories of professional requirements but teaches only the AICPA model: "must", "should", and "may/might/could" as explanatory material that "imposes no requirement". Rule 3101 has a third category, the responsibility to consider. aud-ps-06 ("A standard says the auditor \"may\" consider a factor") names no framework, but its key says the auditor has no obligation beyond understanding the text. The chk2 (d) explanation says "the categories apply in both AICPA and PCAOB standards".
evidence: Rule 3101(a)(3): "may", "might", "could" describe actions and procedures that auditors have a professional obligation to consider; whether and how they are applied depends on professional judgment. Rule 3101(a)(1) also uses "shall" and "is required" for unconditional responsibilities. So under PCAOB standards, aud-ps-06 key (a) ("None beyond understanding it") overstates the point. The AICPA statement (no requirement, but the auditor must understand the entire text, AU-C 200) is correct only for GAAS.
source: PCAOB Rule 3101; AU-C 200.25 and application material
fix: Add a row or sentence to the lesson: "PCAOB Rule 3101 has three categories: unconditional (must, shall, is required), presumptively mandatory (should) and responsibility to consider (may, might, could)." Reword the aud-ps-06 stem to "In the AU-C sections, a standard says the auditor \"may\"...". Change the chk2 (d) explanation to "Both AICPA and PCAOB standards use \"must\" and \"should\"; the PCAOB adds a third category, the responsibility to consider."

fix: Relabel the skill as "remembering" (or "application" at most). Better, make it an application/analysis TBS. Add an exhibit with a file timeline (report date, release date, the date of a late-added memo, a deleted workpaper) and ask the candidate to identify the policy violations.

issue: The time and size estimate is unrealistic. The TBS is set at 15 minutes, but it has 5 recall dropdowns (2 to 4 options each), no exhibits and about 90 words of text. That is about a 3–5 minute task. The planner and mock-time estimates will overstate the study time, and the item is much thinner than an exam docreview TBS. Those usually have one or more exhibits and 6–10 editable phrases. Blank submissions also earn 20%, because p5 is correct as written and scores as correct when left alone (tbsScoring.ts docreview default).
evidence: Word count of the segments is about 90. Options per row: p1 4, p2 3, p3 3, p4 2, p5 3. With no exhibits there is nothing to read beyond the policy text. The 20% figure follows from src/lib/tbsScoring.ts: an untouched segment keeps its original text, so p5 is correct. That is by design and acceptable alone, but on a 5-row TBS it makes up a large share of the score.
source: AICPA AUD sample-test docreview format; src/lib/tbsScoring.ts
fix: Cut minutes to 5–6, or expand the TBS to about 8–10 editable phrases. Add a PCAOB-versus-AICPA contrast and an exhibit (a file-assembly log). That would also support the higher skill label.

issue: Row p4 uses the wrong trigger date, and its explanation uses a third date. The policy sentence says "If documentation is added after the report release date". The explanation says "Additions after the report date must show when, by whom, the reasons and their effect." Under AU-C 230, the "who, when, why and effect" requirement applies to changes after the documentation completion date. New procedures or conclusions after the report date are a separate rule. Administrative additions during the 60-day assembly window (for example, evidence obtained before the report date) do not trigger it. The PCAOB rule (AS 1215.16) does attach to additions after the report release date, so the row blends the two frameworks. That matters because the TBS states that Kessler audits only nonissuers. p4 also has only two options, one of them implausible ("only the new conclusion").
evidence: AU-C 230 (changes after the documentation completion date): "regardless of the nature of the modifications or additions, document (a) when and by whom ... made and, when applicable, reviewed; (b) the specific reasons; (c) the effect, if any, on the auditor's conclusions". AU-C 230 (assembly): administrative changes during final assembly are allowed. The keyed answer is still the better of the two options, so scoring is not wrong.
source: AU-C 230 (assembly, changes after the documentation completion date, matters arising after the report date); PCAOB AS 1215.16
fix: Reword the policy sentence to "If documentation is added or changed after the documentation completion date, the staff member records". Use the options "only the new conclusion | when and by whom it was made and reviewed, the reason, and the effect on conclusions | nothing, if the change is administrative". Change the explanation to "AU-C 230: after the documentation completion date, any change must record when and by whom it was made and reviewed, the specific reasons, and the effect on conclusions."

issue: The wording is imprecise for a module that teaches "must" versus "should". AU-C 230 states these requirements with "should" (presumptively mandatory): "should ... complete the assembly ... no later than 60 days" and "should not delete or discard". The policy text says "must be assembled" and keys "must not be deleted". The instructions say "underlined statement", but the part prompt says "highlighted phrase". The p3 explanation says "AU-C 230 requires retention for at least five years". The five-year minimum is in AU-C 230 application material, which refers to the quality-management standard ("ordinarily no shorter than five years"). The requirement itself is to retain documentation for a period sufficient for the firm's and legal needs.
evidence: AU-C 230 requirements use "should" throughout. The 5-year figure appears in the application material, which refers to QM sec. 10 (SQMS 1).
source: AU-C 230; SQMS No. 1 (QM sec. 10)
fix: Use "should" in the policy sentences and the keyed option ("should not be deleted"), or add a note that a firm policy may make the standard mandatory. Use "highlighted" consistently. p3 explanation: "AU-C 230 application material (with SQMS 1): retention ordinarily no shorter than five years from the report release date (PCAOB: seven years)."

issue: Skill is one level too high: 7 pure-recall items are labelled "application". Each asks for a definition or the name of an issuing body, with no fact pattern to apply. Examples: the meaning of "should", "may" or "must"; the authority of interpretive and other publications; which body issues GAAS; the overall objectives. Their twins carry the correct label. aud-ps-22 ("must", remembering) matches aud-ps-16 ("must", application). aud-ps-21 (ASB, remembering/1) matches aud-ps-19 (ASB, application/2). aud-x1-29 ("should", remembering) matches aud-ps-chk2 ("should", application).
evidence: Same content, different labels: ps-16 vs ps-22; ps-19 vs ps-21; chk2 vs x1-29 and ps-23. Under the Blueprint, remembering and understanding means recalling or recognizing a concept.
source: AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint skill definitions
fix: Relabel aud-ps-chk2, -06, -16, -17, -18, -19 and -20 as remembering. Set difficulty 1 for ps-16 and ps-19.

issue: Heavy redundancy: about half of this module's 33 MCQs repeat another item in the same way. Within the module: "ASB issues GAAS for nonissuers / private-company audits follow AU-C" appears in ps-19, ps-21 and x1-21. "Must = unconditional" appears in ps-16 and ps-22. "Should = presumptively mandatory" appears in chk2, ps-23 and x1-29, so "must"/"should" terminology is tested in 5 items plus flashcard f5. "Document a departure" appears in ps-10 and ps-24. "Report may cite both GAAS and PCAOB" appears in ps-14 and ps-25. Across modules: ps-12 matches aud-gov-22 (same stem, GAO issues the Yellow Book). ps-13 matches aud-ev-19 (same supplier-confirmation scenario). ps-27 is a fourth copy of the AU-C 585 "assess first" item (aud-se-03, aud-se-13, aud-x3-25).
evidence: Jaccard similarity of stems: ps-22 ~ ps-23 = 0.71; ps-14 ~ ps-25 = 0.50; ps-12 ~ aud-gov-22 = 0.75; ps-13 ~ aud-ev-19 = 0.59; ps-27 ~ aud-se-13 = 0.53 and ~ aud-x3-25 = 0.50. ps-19 and ps-21 have the same stem in different words. The keys are identical in each cluster. Several clusters exceed the guide of 3 times. Meanwhile, high-yield framework topics get no item: SSARS vs. AU-C 930 for interim reviews, PCAOB for broker-dealers, AS 1000 responsibilities, unconscious biases beyond anchoring (only ps-11).
source: Review brief §2 duplicates rule
fix: Keep one item per cluster (for example ps-21, ps-22 or ps-23, ps-24, ps-14). Remove ps-27 (or move it to aud-subsequent-events) and either ps-12 or aud-gov-22. Replace the cut items with new scenario items: confirmation-bias and automation-bias scenarios; an interim review of a nonissuer audit client (AU-C 930); a broker-dealer audit (PCAOB); a PCAOB "may" (responsibility to consider); the inherent limitations of an audit vs. a review.

issue: Mock exam aud-mock-3 contains both aud-x1-10 ("Which statement is true regarding reasonable assurance?", key "a high level of assurance, but not absolute") and aud-x1-32 ("reasonable assurance, which means:", key "A high, but not absolute, level of assurance"). They are the same item twice on one form: each one gives away the other's answer, and one fact counts double toward the mock score.
evidence: grep of content/aud/exams/aud-mock-3.json finds "aud-x1-12" "aud-x1-10" "aud-x1-29" "aud-x1-32". Both keys say "high, but not absolute". Distractors repeat too: (a) absolute assurance; review-level assurance in x1-10 (c) and x1-32 (b).
source: Review brief §2.6 (one item revealing the answer to another) and §2.7
fix: Replace aud-x1-32 in aud-mock-3 with a different Area I item, or rewrite aud-x1-32 to test a different point, for example "Which is an inherent limitation of an audit?" (persuasive, not conclusive, evidence).

issue: Answer cues and weak distractors let a test-wise candidate answer without knowing the rule. ps-14 and ps-25: every distractor carries an absolute ("only", "always", "must not"), and the key repeats the stem's "both". ps-20: two distractors are absolutes ("Absolute assurance of no errors", "Detecting all fraud of any size") and the third ("Preparing the financial statements") is implausible. ps-24: distractor (a) "Nothing; it's optional" contradicts the stem's "presumptively mandatory". ps-27: the key ("Assess its effect") is the only measured option; the others say "Nothing", "at once" or "immediately". x1-29: the key is the only option without "every case", "without documentation" or "only".
evidence: cues.md flags each of these, and I confirmed each by reading the options. ps-27 omits the most tempting real-world error: performing the omitted procedure right away, before assessing its importance (AU-C 585 requires the assessment first).
source: Review brief §2.6
fix: ps-14/25 (if both are kept): use distractors such as "As GAAS only, because the entity is a nonissuer", "As PCAOB standards only, because they are more stringent", "Both, but only if the PCAOB registers the engagement". ps-27: replace (a) or (d) with "Promptly perform the omitted procedure" and "Notify persons relying on the report". ps-20: use "Reasonable assurance that the FS are free of all misstatements, material or not" and "Expressing an opinion on internal control". ps-24: replace (a) with "Disclose the departure in the auditor's report". x1-29: use "A requirement the auditor may depart from whenever an alternative is more efficient".

issue: Several trap labels do not match the misconception. The label "partial-computation" is used on non-computational items: ps-08 (a) "GAAS only" (an incomplete rule set), ps-10 (a) "Nothing further, because the alternative is better", and ps-14 (b) "Only as PCAOB standards". In ps-03, a NOT question, distractors (a)–(c) are true statements of the audit premise but are labelled "wrong-rule". The misconception there is missing the negation, or treating a true premise element as the exception.
evidence: None of these items has calc=true or any arithmetic. The available labels include wrong-rule, overgeneralization, reversed and other (src/content/schema.ts TRAP_TYPES).
source: src/content/schema.ts TRAP_TYPES
fix: ps-08 (a): wrong-rule. ps-10 (a): wrong-rule. ps-14 (b): wrong-rule (or overgeneralization). ps-03 (a)–(c): reversed (or other).

issue: Distractor (d) "Due professional care" is also violated on a reasonable reading. The stem asks "Which concept has been violated?" Due professional care includes professional skepticism, so accepting an explanation without corroboration violates both. The choice explanation concedes it is "Related".
evidence: PCAOB AS 1000 (due professional care) requires professional skepticism. The former AU 230 / AS 1015 said due professional care requires the auditor to exercise professional skepticism. (a) is the most specific answer, but the stem does not ask for the most specific one.
source: PCAOB AS 1000; AU-C 200 (professional skepticism)
fix: Reword the stem: "Which concept has the auditor most directly failed to apply?" Or replace (d) with a clearly wrong concept, such as "Professional judgment in setting materiality".

issue: Distractor (b) "Signing the audit report on the date the letter says" is unclear: which letter? Its explanation, "Dating follows a requirement, not judgment", is also questionable. The report date is the date on which the auditor has obtained sufficient appropriate evidence, and deciding that date takes judgment. A careful candidate could see judgment in (b), and in (c) (deciding which representations to request), which blurs a question meant to have one clear answer.
evidence: AU-C 700: the report is dated no earlier than the date on which the auditor has obtained sufficient appropriate audit evidence, which is itself a judgment. No standard dates the report on a date set by "the letter".
source: AU-C 700 (date of the auditor's report); AU-C 200 (professional judgment)
fix: Replace (b) with a clearly mechanical step, such as "Footing the trial balance provided by the client". Or reword it: "Dating the report on the date the engagement letter specifies, regardless of when evidence was obtained", and explain why that violates AU-C 700.

issue: The key "Consider and apply them" overstates the duty to follow interpretive publications. The difference between the key and distractor (a), "Follow them as requirements", is thin and slightly misleading. The rule is that the auditor should consider applicable interpretive publications, and if one is not applied, should be prepared to explain how the related GAAS requirements were met. Applying them is not mandatory.
evidence: AU-C 200 application material: interpretive publications are not auditing standards. They are recommendations on how to apply GAAS. The auditor should consider them and, if not applying the guidance, be prepared to explain how GAAS was complied with. The item's own overall explanation says this correctly, but the key text does not.
source: AU-C 200 (interpretive publications)
fix: Key text: "Consider them; if not applied, be prepared to explain how GAAS was met". Choice explanation: "Correct. Interpretive publications are recommendations, not requirements, but the auditor must be able to justify not applying them."

issue: Explanations are thin, circular or garbled. chk1 (d): "SSAEs govern attestation engagements on subject matter other than historical statements under SSARS" is hard to parse; it reads as if SSARS covered the subject matter. ps-16 (b) "Correct. It must be complied with." and ps-22 (b) "Correct. It must always be followed." restate the stem with no source and no contrast with "should". ps-18 (d) "Correct. They have no authoritative status." repeats the key. ps-25: the choice and overall explanations ("The report may refer to both") restate the key and give no rule or citation.
evidence: None of these explanations cites a source (AU-C 200.25, AU-C 200 application material, AU-C 700) or says why the rule exists. Brief §2.4 says explanations must state the rule and not be circular.
source: Review brief §2.4
fix: chk1 (d): "SSAEs (AT-C 210) cover reviews of subject matter other than historical financial statements; a review of a nonissuer's historical FS is under SSARS (AR-C 90)." ps-16/22 (b): "AU-C 200.25: \"must\" = unconditional; there is no departure even in rare circumstances, unlike \"should\"." ps-18 (d): "AU-C 200: other auditing publications (textbooks, journal articles, CPE) have no authoritative status but may help the auditor understand and apply GAAS." ps-25: cite AU-C 700 and explain when the report may refer to both sets of standards.

issue: The lesson has one pre-question (aud-ps-pre1, management's responsibility) for four objectives. Nothing primes the must/should categories or the bias content, which are the parts learners most often get wrong. The fourth objective (biases) also has no Blueprint task link, though Blueprint Area I group B, "Professional skepticism and professional judgment", covers it directly.
evidence: Frontmatter has preQuestions: [aud-ps-pre1]. Objective 4 has no task field. The bias table is tested by only one item (aud-ps-11, anchoring).
source: AICPA 2026 AUD Blueprint Area I.B
fix: Add a pre-question such as "A standard says the auditor \"should\" do X. Can the auditor ever skip it?" Add task "Recognize impediments to professional skepticism, including unconscious biases" to objective 4. Add one item each on confirmation bias and automation bias.

issue: Systematic skill/difficulty mislabel: every item from far-gov-21 to far-gov-31 is labeled skill 'analysis' and difficulty 3, but each is a one-fact recall or a one-step application. Several are pure recall labeled analysis (two levels off), and far-gov-26 is also flagged calc:true with no computation.
evidence: All 10 'analysis' labels in the module sit on items 21-31, and each of those items is difficulty 3. Recall items labeled analysis: far-gov-22 (compensated absences recognized when due), far-gov-27 (bond proceeds = other financing source; the near-identical far-gov-16 is labeled application/2), far-gov-31 (DB plan assets -> pension trust fund), far-gov-26 (capital outlay = GF expenditure / government-wide asset; far-gov-03 and -12 test the same facts at application/2) and far-gov-28 (principal repayment reduces the liability government-wide). One-step application items labeled analysis: far-gov-21 (sign of one reconciling item), far-gov-24 (900,000 + 40,000; the harder exam twin far-x1-17 with uncollectibles is application/2), far-gov-25 (500,000 - 300,000 - 50,000), far-gov-29 (60,000 / 5) and far-gov-30 (5,000,000 - 3,000,000; the identical far-gov-23 is application/2). No item examines interrelationships or draws conclusions from several data sources, which is what the Blueprint means by Analysis. The labels also inflate the module's analysis share (10 of 31 practice items) and make the easy-to-hard progression artificial.
source: AICPA Uniform CPA Examination Blueprints, skill-level definitions (Remembering & Understanding / Application / Analysis)
fix: Relabel: far-gov-21 application/2; -22 remembering/2; -24 application/2; -25 application/2; -26 application/1 with calc:false; -27 remembering/1 (or delete it as a duplicate of -16); -28 application/2; -29 application/2; -30 application/2 (or delete it as a duplicate of -23); -31 remembering/1.

issue: Seven practice MCQs test government mechanics that the 2024+ Blueprints place in BAR Area III. They cover budgetary entries, encumbrances, interfund transfers, fund-to-government-wide reconciliation and compensated-absence liabilities. None is marked optional, and the lesson never teaches any of them, so they count toward FAR readiness while drilling untaught, off-Blueprint content.
evidence: Reference sheets: blueprint-notes FAR I.C says state and local government is 'foundational only: the ACFR, measurement focus, basis of accounting, fund types and net position. Full government accounting is BAR Area III.' far-standards §1c lists for BAR 'deriving government-wide statements and the reconciliations, specific transactions (capital assets, long-term liabilities, interfund activity, nonexchange revenue, budgetary and encumbrance entries)'. SuperFastCPA files the reconciliation and fund-balance computations as BAR tasks ('BAR CPA Exam: How to prepare a schedule to reconcile fund balances ... to net position in government-wide statements'; 'BAR CPA Exam: How to Calculate the Fund Balances ... and Prepare Journal Entries'). Lesson check: it never mentions budgets, appropriations, encumbrances, transfers or compensated absences, and for the reconciliation it says only 'a reconciliation between the two is required' (worked insight), with no adjustments taught. far-gov-18, for example, needs + capital outlay - depreciation - bond proceeds + principal repaid (-100,000 + 2,000,000 - 600,000 - 3,000,000 + 500,000 = -1,200,000). That is 7 of 31 practice items (23%).
source: AICPA 2026 FAR/BAR Blueprints (FAR I.C vs BAR III), per review/reference/blueprint-notes.md and far-standards.md §1c; https://www.superfastcpa.com/bar-cpa-exam-how-to-prepare-a-schedule-to-reconcile-fund-balances-in-the-governmental-financial-statements-to-net-position-in-government-wide-statements/
fix: Mark far-gov-13, -15, -18, -20, -21, -22 and -25 optional:true, as REVIEW.md P2-2 did for the other off-Blueprint items, or move them to BAR content. Backfill with in-scope FAR items (for example: statement of activities net (expense) revenue and program vs. general revenues; what the government-wide statements include and exclude; deferred inflows of resources; proprietary vs. fiduciary statement names). If any item is kept as core, add the matching lesson section.

issue: Lesson-item alignment gap for in-scope content. The lesson names the fund types only in a diagram and never says what special revenue, debt service, capital projects, custodial or investment trust funds are for. Items and all three TBS ask the learner to classify activities into exactly those funds. RSI contents and the treatment of debt principal are also tested but not taught.
evidence: The mermaid diagram (lines 57-73) gives a purpose only for enterprise, internal service, permanent and private-purpose trust funds. Items that need the missing definitions: far-gov-02; far-tbs-r3-property-tax rows a2-a4 (capital projects, special revenue, debt service); far-tbs-u4-government-plans rows c, d, e (special revenue, debt service, custodial for taxes collected for a school district); far-tbs-x1-government rows f1, f2, f5, f7. far-gov-17 asks which items are RSI, but the lesson lists RSI only as a component of the ACFR (MD&A is listed separately and nothing says it is RSI). far-gov-19 and -28 need 'principal repayment is an expenditure in the fund and reduces the liability government-wide'. The lesson says only 'debt service recognized when due'.
source: GASB 54 ¶¶29-35 (governmental fund type definitions); GASB 84 (custodial funds); GASB 34 ¶8 as amended by GASB 103 (MD&A and RSI)
fix: Add a 'What each fund is for' table with one line and one example per fund type. Use GASB 54 wording for special revenue (restricted or committed revenue sources that make up a substantial portion of inflows), capital projects, debt service and permanent funds, plus custodial vs. trust funds. Add one sentence that MD&A and budgetary comparison schedules are RSI, and one that debt principal paid is a fund expenditure but reduces bonds payable government-wide.

issue: The net investment in capital assets definition ('capital assets, net of depreciation, minus related debt') omits the unspent-proceeds rule. In the lesson's own worked example the rule gives a wrong figure.
evidence: Worked example: $2,000,000 of bonds, $1,500,000 spent on a fire station, $500,000 unspent at December 31. Applying the lesson's rule: 1,500,000 - 2,000,000 = -500,000 NICA. Under GASB 63 ¶9 (Cod. 2200.118), the portion of debt attributable to unspent proceeds is excluded from NICA and goes into the same component as the unspent proceeds (here restricted). So NICA = 1,500,000 - 1,500,000 = 0, and the remaining 500,000 debt offsets the 500,000 restricted cash. Deferred outflows and inflows attributable to capital debt are also part of the definition.
source: GASB Statement 63 ¶9; GASB Codification 2200.118
fix: Amend line 87: 'capital assets net of accumulated depreciation, minus the outstanding debt (and related deferred outflows/inflows) attributable to acquiring or building them; debt proceeds not yet spent are excluded.' Optionally add a step to the worked example showing NICA = 0 and restricted net position = 0 (500,000 cash - 500,000 related debt).

issue: Duplicate and near-duplicate practice items: five items repeat another item's fact in the same way, taking slots from untested in-scope topics.
evidence: far-gov-11 has the same stem as far-gov-01 (automated Jaccard 1.00) with the same answer content; only the letter moves. far-gov-27 is far-gov-16 again: $5,000,000 bond proceeds received by a capital projects fund -> other financing source. The same fact is also in far-gov-pre1, far-gov-fc7 and the lesson big idea. far-gov-30 is far-gov-23 with different numbers (net capital assets - related debt). far-gov-14 is far-gov-04 (inventory -> nonspendable). far-gov-26 merges far-gov-03 (truck = fund expenditure) and far-gov-12 (truck capitalized government-wide). Meanwhile no item covers program vs. general revenues, the statement of activities format, major funds, component units, deferred outflows/inflows, or proprietary and fiduciary statement names.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 7 (duplicates/redundancy)
fix: Delete far-gov-11, -27 and -30, and replace -14 and -26 with new in-scope items. Suggested topics: net (expense) revenue by function and program revenues (charges for services, operating/capital grants) vs. general revenues (taxes); what government-wide statements exclude (fiduciary) and how internal service funds fold into governmental activities; deferred inflows of resources; the names of proprietary and fiduciary fund statements.

issue: Practice items reappear almost verbatim on mock exams, and mock 3 tests the 60-day property tax rule three times. A learner who did the practice set sees recognition items on the mock, and one mock item cues another.
evidence: far-gov-24 (practice): $1,000,000 levy, $900,000 collected, $40,000 within 60 days -> $940,000. far-x1-17 (exam, on far-mock-1 and far-mock-3) has the same $1,000,000 / $900,000 / $40,000 and the same $940,000 key. far-tbs-r3-property-tax (practice) and far-tbs-x1-government (exam, on far-mock-3) share a $5,000,000 levy, 2% uncollectible and the same fund-classification rows: utility -> enterprise, bond proceeds -> capital projects, gas tax -> special revenue, GO debt -> debt service, motor pool -> internal service, park endowment -> permanent. far-mock-3 contains far-x1-17, far-x1-35 and the TBS pt part, all testing 60-day availability, and the far-x1-17 stem ('expects to collect $40,000 within 60 days after year-end') cues the answer to far-x1-35.
source: Review brief §2 per-MCQ check 6 (one item revealing another) and 7 (duplicates); content/far/exams/far-mock-1.json, far-mock-3.json
fix: Change the figures in far-gov-24 (for example a $2,400,000 levy) and change the activities and levy in far-tbs-r3-property-tax (for example a special assessment, an airport, an investment pool). On far-mock-3, replace far-x1-35 or far-x1-17 with an in-scope item on a different concept (for example fiduciary exclusion or net position components).

issue: Optional-scope flags are inconsistent. far-gov-04, -05 and -08 are optional under REVIEW.md's 'GASB fund balance' decision, but the same facts stay core elsewhere. far-gov-05 is not a fund balance item at all: it tests net position, which the Blueprint notes put inside FAR I.C.
evidence: far-gov-04 (inventory -> nonspendable) is optional, while far-gov-14 (inventory and prepaids -> nonspendable) is core. far-gov-08 (only the general fund has positive unassigned) is optional, while the lesson objective 3, key takeaway 6, far-gov-fc5, far-gov-chk2, far-gov-13 and far-tbs-u4-government-plans part fb all teach or test GASB 54 fund balance as core. far-gov-05 (definition of net investment in capital assets) is optional, while far-gov-23 and -30 (the NICA computation) and far-gov-fc4 are core. blueprint-notes I.C lists 'net position' as FAR foundational content. REVIEW.md lists the decision as 'P2-2, confirm' (unconfirmed), and the cited coverage-FAR.md does not exist in the repo.
source: REVIEW.md 'Optional off-Blueprint material (P2-2, confirm)'; review/reference/blueprint-notes.md FAR I.C
fix: Check the FAR I.C representative tasks in the official 2026 FAR Blueprint, then apply one rule. If fund balance classification is BAR, also mark far-gov-14, -13 and fc5 optional, add an optional note to the lesson's fund balance section and objective, and move the TBS fb part to a BAR/optional TBS. In either case remove optional from far-gov-05 (net position is FAR). If fund balance is FAR, remove optional from far-gov-04 and -08 too.

issue: The availability rule is worded loosely as 'collected within (about) 60 days'. It leaves out 'during the year or' and/or 'after year-end', so read literally the keyed option excludes taxes collected earlier in the year.
evidence: far-x1-35 key (a): 'Levied for 2025 and collected within 60 days'. Within 60 days of what? Read literally, a 2025 tax collected in March 2025 does not qualify, yet it is revenue. far-gov-07 key (c): '(collected within about 60 days)'. far-gov-fc6 back: 'collected within ~60 days after year-end' omits collections during the year. far-gov-24 choice (a) rationale: 'Revenue is collected within 60 days.' By contrast, the glossary ('Available (modified accrual)': 'Collected within the period or soon enough afterward (generally 60 days...)') and the lesson (line 53) state the rule correctly. Under GASB Cod. P70, available means collected within the current period or expected to be collected soon enough thereafter to pay current liabilities, not to exceed 60 days.
source: NCGA Interpretation 3 / GASB Codification P70.104; GASB 33
fix: Reword far-x1-35 (a) to 'Levied for 2025 and collected during 2025 or within 60 days after year-end', and far-gov-07 (c) to 'When measurable and available (collected during the year or within 60 days after year-end)'. Make fc6 read '...collected during the year or within 60 days after year-end'. Make far-gov-24 (a) read 'Correct. 900,000 collected during the year + 40,000 collected within 60 days after year-end.'

issue: The exam TBS never states the availability period. The pt answers (revenue 4,700,000, deferred inflows 200,000) work only if the learner assumes a 60-day period, while the practice twin far-tbs-r3-property-tax states it.
evidence: Exhibit: collected 4,500,000 in 2025; 200,000 collected January 1 - February 28, 2026; 200,000 later in 2026. Key: rev = 4,500,000 + 200,000 = 4,700,000 and def = 4,900,000 - 4,700,000 = 200,000 (recomputed: 5,000,000 × 98% = 4,900,000). Both rows assume collections through February 28 (59 days) are 'available'. GASB sets 60 days as a ceiling ('not to exceed 60 days'), and each government discloses its own period. With a 30-day policy, for example, the answer changes.
source: GASB Codification P70.104 (property taxes: available = collected within 60 days after year-end, not to exceed)

issue: Distractor rationales are thin or circular ('Not the computation.', 'Not the treatment.'), and several trap labels don't match the misconception the distractor models.

issue: Neither the lesson nor far-gov-17 mentions GASB 103 (Financial Reporting Model Improvements), which applies to fiscal years beginning after June 15, 2025 and is testable throughout 2026. It changes several 'format and content' points that sit in FAR's foundational scope.
evidence: The lesson citations list GASB 34, 54 and 84 and Cod. 1100/1300/2200, with no GASB 103. far-gov-17's explanation cites 'GASB 34: MD&A and budgetary comparison schedules (among others) are RSI'. Under GASB 34 the budgetary comparison could instead be presented as a basic statement. GASB 103 makes it RSI only, requires variance columns, sets five MD&A sections, replaces extraordinary and special items with separately presented unusual or infrequent items, and adds the proprietary-fund subtotal 'operating income (loss) and noncapital subsidies'. The keys are still correct.
source: GASB Statement 103 (issued 2024; FY beginning after 6/15/2025), per review/reference/far-standards.md §4b and 'GASB 103 in detail'
fix: Add GASB 103 to the lesson citations and a short ACFR note: MD&A (five required sections) and the budgetary comparison for the general fund and major special revenue funds are RSI. Cite 'GASB 34 as amended by GASB 103' in far-gov-17.

issue: The GASB 54 fund balance table is slightly incomplete. 'Assigned' omits intent expressed by the governing body itself and omits the rule that positive residuals in other governmental funds are assigned. 'Committed' omits that the constraint is removed only by the same type of action.

fix: Assigned: 'Intended use set by the governing body or by a body or official it has delegated; also all positive residual fund balance in governmental funds other than the general fund.' Committed: add 'removed or changed only by the same formal action'.

issue: The AU-C 505 conditions for using negative confirmations as the sole substantive procedure are listed differently in each place. Only aud-x3-33 includes the requirement that evidence on the operating effectiveness of controls has been obtained; the lesson, flashcard and aud-rev-23 drop it, and the lesson says negative requests are 'used only when' the conditions hold (the conditions govern using them ALONE, not using them at all).
evidence: aud-x3-33 explanation: 'Negative confirmations alone are appropriate when RMM is low and controls are effective, the population has many small homogeneous balances, a low exception rate is expected, and recipients are expected to read them.' Lesson L36: 'negative requests ... used only when RMM is low, there are many small, homogeneous balances, few exceptions are expected, and recipients are expected to read them.'
